newsitem.title: NORWAY: NORDIC SKIING-NORWAY LEAD COMBINED EVENT AFTER JUMPING.
newsitem.headline: NORDIC SKIING-NORWAY LEAD COMBINED EVENT AFTER JUMPING.

text.p: Norway opened up an early lead in Wednesday's Nordic combined team event at the Nordic skiing world championships after the ski jumping competition.
Two brilliant jumps of 93.5 and 94 metres by Bjarte Engen Vik helped the home country score a total of 908.5 points which will enable them to start the 4x5-km relay later on Wednesday in front.
Vik and team mates Halldor Skard, Fred Boerre Lundberg and Knut Tore Apeland will set off seven seconds before Finland, second on 904 points in the provisional standings.
The Czechs, third on 899.5 points, will start 15 seconds after the Norwegians.
There was disappointment for Japan, the world and Olympic champions, who were a modest sixth and will start the relay with a 72-second handicap behind Norway.
Kenji Ogiwara, who took the individual title on Sunday, was partly to blame for his team's poor performance with a modest first jump of 82 metres followed by a second of 88.5 metres.
